title: Gradual traffic decoupling for LTS and canary cohorts
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a controlled, decoupled traffic-ramping mechanism that supports LTS channels, staged canaries, and feature-flag driven cohorts so we can safely roll runtime and model changes across regions and tenant tiers. This ticket covers the engineering design and implementation of the traffic decoupling layer, rollout gate integration, and an automated rollback webhook for unsafe regressions.

Motivation: Current rollout tooling mixes model and runtime routing, making cross-version rollouts brittle for LTS consumers and per-customer dedicated pools. We need a routing shim that can: (1) pin traffic by channel (lts/stable/edge), (2) support percentage ramps across multiple cohorts simultaneously, (3) integrate with our feature-flag system for cohort selection, and (4) emit deterministic signals for the rollback operator.

Scope:
- Lightweight routing shim in the API edge that maps incoming requests into cohorts (by channel, feature-flag, tenancy, or region).
- Percent-based traffic controller service that can schedule ramps and honor hard safety gates.
- Gate evaluation engine that consumes telemetry and signals (error-rate, latency p95/p99, token-quality regression from eval service) and triggers automated rollback or pause.
- DevOps hooks: CLI and Console UI endpoints to create ramps, cancel, or escalate to manual approval.
- Telemetry and dashboards for cohort-level SLOs and regression detection.
- Runbook and chaos-testing plan for simulated bad releases.

Out of scope: cross-data-center capacity autoscaling (handled by Dedicated team), detailed UX polish in Console (follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Traffic shim can split traffic by channel and feature-flag and persist cohort assignments for sticky sessions.
2) Percent-based ramp can be scheduled via CICD or Console and run for multiple cohorts concurrently.
3) Gate engine evaluates metrics every 30s and can auto-pause/rollback to previous model/runtime within 2 minutes of violation.
4) Post-rollback, system creates an incident artifact including telemetry snapshot and links to the rollback PR.
5) Integration tests simulate a regression (increased token-error rate) and verify automatic rollback path in staging.
6) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console's rollout UI.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 - Staging: deploy shim and gate engine to staging; run simulated regressions using synthetic workload.
Phase 1 - Internal canary: 0.1% traffic for internal tenants for 24h with strict gates.
Phase 2 - External canary: 1% traffic across 10% of production tenants, monitor 48h.
Phase 3 - LTS-aware ramp: enable LTS channel pinning; ramp stable consumers in 5% increments with 4-hour windows.
Phase 4 - Gradual release: open up to 100% with automated rollback enabled.
Notes: All ramps require a minimum healthy capacity check and circuit-breaker fallback to previous variant. Ramps are defined as percentage deltas per cohort and are additive across independent cohorts (e.g., canary + regional shard).
gating_thresholds:
Primary gates:
- Error rate (4xx/5xx combined): alarm if >0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 5m.
- Latency: p99 increase >25% or p95 increase >40% over baseline for 5m.
- Token-quality regressions: eval-run mismatch score delta >1.0 (per prompt-set) over 30m.
- Resource saturation: GPU utilization >90% sustained for 2m or OOMs observed.
Behavior: If any primary gate trips, gate engine will: 1) pause ramp, 2) reduce cohort to last safe percentage, 3) if critical (error spike or OOM), trigger auto-rollback to last promoted variant and create rollback incident.
Secondary gates (informational): anomaly in tracing error classes, elevated retries, or increased cache-miss rate. Secondary gates surface in dashboards and ping on-call but do not auto-rollback.
implementation_notes:
Decisions so far:
- Use existing feature-flag provider for cohort selection to avoid a new plumbing.
- Implement percentage controller as independent stateless worker that writes cohort percentages to a consistent store (Redis with raft-backed failover) to reduce API-edge state.
- Gate engine will subscribe to metric streams (prometheus pushgateway + Kafka events for token-quality) and evaluate rules in a WASM-based sandbox for configurable policies.
Tradeoffs:
- Storing cohort assignment in Redis gives sticky routing but increases cross-AZ calls; alternate approach was header-based sticky tokens, rejected due to multi-proxy re-writing complexity.
- WASM sandbox adds complexity but allows non-dev teams to author gate policies safely.
Open questions:
- Should LTS consumers be opt-out (pinned) by default or opt-in to receive upgrades? Recommendation: opt-in with explicit migration windows for LTS.
- Final SLA for auto-rollback latency (currently targeting 2 mins) — needs legal sign-off for enterprise SLAs.

2025-09-09 - On-call test run: injected synthetic 2x error rate into staging; gate engine paused ramp and initiated rollback sequence as expected. Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Simulated-Rollback-2025-09-09.
